> > this looked cute so I tried it, but it breaks serialization in LangServe streaming events (`RemoteRunnable.astream_events`) because the `NodeType`'s value object is set as a key along the `data` object of `on_chain_stream` and `WellKnownLCSerializer.dumps` doesn't like that > > Thanks for the feedback, it was something I hadn't noticed, could you provide more detailed code to help me understand the problem more clearly, it will help us to think more fully. it's basically as you had shared; compile the graph to a Runnable and provide to LangServe `add_routes` to expose as a route:
demo_server.py ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request from langserve import add_routes # your example compiled workflow from example import app as workflow app = FastAPI( title="LangChain Server", version="1.0", description="Spin up a simple api server using Langchain's Runnable interfaces", ) add_routes(app, workflow, path="/example") if __name__ == "__main__": import uvicorn uvicorn.run(app, host="localhost", port=8000) ```
then on client side I put together this little utility REPL:
demo_remote_runnable.py ```python import pprint import asyncio from enum import StrEnum from uuid import uuid4 from langserve import RemoteRunnable from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage class Commands(StrEnum): NEW_THREAD = "new thread" OLD_THREAD = "prev thread" DEBUG_ENABLE = "debug" class Modes(StrEnum): STREAM = "stream_async" GENERATE_EVENTS = "generate_events" async def prompt(): while True: try: _prompt = input("Human: ") except EOFError: break if _prompt == "q": print("Exiting...") break yield _prompt async def run(): runner = RemoteRunnable( url=f"http://localhost:8000/example", ) # NOTE: default ON for purpose of example and also I haven't finished this next part debug: bool = True user_id = str(uuid4()) thread_id = str(uuid4()) prev_thread: str = "" async for user_input in prompt(): if user_input == Commands.NEW_THREAD: prev_thread = thread_id thread_id = str(uuid4()) continue elif user_input == Commands.OLD_THREAD: prev_thread, thread_id = (thread_id, prev_thread) continue elif user_input == Commands.DEBUG_ENABLE: debug = not debug continue print("...") try: async for event in runner.astream_events( input={"input": user_input}, config={ "configurable": { "user_id": user_id, "thread_id": thread_id, }, "run_name": "Test Run", "metadata": {"remote_meta": "test"}, }, version="v1", include_names=["/example"], ): if debug: pprint.pp(event) # TODO: format the event stream into something more fun and exciting to look at in a demo video :/ except Exception as e: print(f"Whoopsy doodle, something broke :(\n{e}") print("\n---") if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(run()) ```

body:
Thanks for the PR! will have to discuss this with @nfcampos before landing something here. I think it would be counter-intuitive to eagerly consume the generator in the serializer, so at a glance it seems preferable for now to crash (aka not support generators in the state) and let the user decide transparently how to handle vs. trying to guess for them.

There's a few gotchas:

1. Generator could be infinite - we may never finish this / crash anyway
2. Generators may take long to consume - if the developer is returning a generator vs. returning a list, it's likely they're doing that for performance reasons
3. If we consume while serializing, need to ensure that  the state serde doesn't impact the graph execution (would need to `tee` it at least I think, since we don't want the consumed generator to then be unavailable in the next node)

Basically, though I may be overthinking this, right now I'm biased to prefer handling generators only explicitly via annotations or something else vs. automatically consuming them.


This PR does raise some interesting questions though. Are you using generators so you can do something more akin to LATS where you start processing in node T+1 while node T is still doing work?

body:
@sangmandu

The `content` of `ToolMessage` itself accepts `str` or `list[str]`, so if your tool outputs a `list[str]`, it won't execute `_stringify`.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33c7f1bb-1036-4531-bfd7-4ebb679096ce)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1fd4569-6270-41c2-8534-6d2e6b874f90)

At this point, the content of `tool_message` remains in UTF-8. Then,
`ToolNode` forcibly converts all results to `str`, ultimately causing the output to become ASCII.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ccaf692-6302-4694-8f6e-772412bc6131)

---

I also noticed the TODO marker and agree that the `_stringify` function in `langchain_core/tool/base.py` should consider incorporating the same changes.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3e291f2-f554-4018-817a-e18d1c76b099)

However, this change to the core won't affect the issue of `list[str]` becoming ASCII here.
As mentioned earlier, it bypassed execution of `_stringify` due to detection.

body:
If you have cycles: 

```python
import json
from langgraph.graph import MessagesState


def call_tools(state: MessagesState):
    tools_by_name = {tool.name: tool for tool in tools}
    messages = state["messages"]
    last_message = messages[-1]
    output_messages = []
    for tool_call in last_message.tool_calls:
        # call the tools
        tool_result = tools_by_name[tool_call["name"]].invoke(tool_call["args"])
        output_messages.append(
            # wrap the tool call results in a ToolMessage.
            # model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic expect any AIMessages with
            # tool calls to be followed by ToolMessages with the tool call results.
            ToolMessage(
                content=json.dumps(tool_result),
                name=tool_call["name"],
                tool_call_id=tool_call["id"],
            )
        )
    return {"messages": output_messages}
```

I'd recommend pushing code blocks like that through an llm to add brief documentation between most lines -- we have wide readership: 

These snippets can be less obvious for folks unfamiliar with what's going on:

```python
    tools_by_name = {tool.name: tool for tool in tools}
    messages = state["messages"]
    last_message = messages[-1] # Why last message?
```

```python
    for tool_call in last_message.tool_calls: # Why multiple?
```

Why so many `[`, why invoke can be used `.invoke`, what's ["args"] and ["name"]

```python
      tool_result = tools_by_name[tool_call["name"]].invoke(tool_call["args"])
```

nits:

> LangGraph allows you to persist data across **multiple threads**. For instance, you can store information about users (their names or preferences) in a shared memory and reuse them in the new conversational threads.

*multiple threads* -> *different threads*
* new conversational threads * -> *new conversations*

"thread" terminology is very obscure so likely link the first mention of thread to the appropriate conceptual page

> When creating a LangGraph workflow, you can set it up to store and retrieve memories by using the [Store](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/store/#langgraph.store.base.BaseStore) interface:

When using the functional API maybe?  `workflow` is another term and it's unclear whether it's a concrete thing or an abstract thing (users will wonder if there's a workflow primitive)


> In this guide, we will show how to construct and use a workflow that has a shared memory implemented using the [Store](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/store/#langgraph.store.base.BaseStore) interface.

Cut boiler plate 

"we will show how to construct and use a workflow" -> "we will create a workflow"


"shared memory implemented" -> "shared memory" sounds like a new term. Is it the same thing as cross thread or different?


Terms used that have the same meaning:

*across threads*
*cross-thread*
*shared memory*

body:
> Hi, this would change langgraph to be a library for DAGs, which is very much the opposite of what we want, as we started langgraph with the explicit goal of supporting graphs with cycles

@nfcampos 
Thank you for your comment. I believe these two aspects do not conflict. My configuration is designed to accommodate custom workflow configuration scenarios. When workflow_mode is not set to True, all operations will continue to function as before, thereby extending the use cases of langgraph. Regarding the issue of graph cycles you mentioned, they are still supported in my project. I integrate looping functionality within subgraphs by predefining certain nodes to handle loop operations.

My goal is to provide clients with low-code workflow configuration capabilities, offering functional nodes that users can freely arrange and combine as needed, without requiring programmers to manually write specific processes.

In my practical tests, I found that only condition_edges had discrepancies with the actual execution results. To address this, I temporarily fixed the issue using a monkey patch. However, I recognize that this is not a long-term solution, which is why I submitted this PR to provide a more robust fix. For example, as shown in my previous example, I simply added a D node after the B node. This does not change the overall execution logic of the workflow, yet it results in completely different execution outcomes. Specifically, whether the E node executes once or twice depends not on the actual execution logic but on whether the number of nodes following the B and C nodes is consistent. I believe this execution behavior is not rigorous. These changes aim to provide a clearer and more reliable execution path for workflows.

In fact,in my usage scenario, both langgraph with workflow_mode and langgraph without workflow_mode coexist simultaneously. The workflow is inherently a tool for user-defined processes, functioning similarly to other tools by providing output based on given input data. The PR I submitted is solely intended to fix issues in the original langgraph during workflow execution. Ultimately, the tools are invoked within agents, where the timing and repetition of calls are managed by the agent's langgraph (langgraph without workflow_mode). These two versions of langgraph can exist concurrently and operate completely independently without interfering with each other.

body:
@andrestorres123 a few changes before we can merge this in.

Take a look at the guidelines for prebuilt agents: https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/prebuilt/#contributing-your-library

* Could you document in the README.md file how to use the package? It only explains what it does, but there's no usage information.
* The package needs to be published on pypi, so it could be used as a library. (There's a breeze package, but it's not clear that it matches the repo).
* Could you update pyproject.toml (author) and license in your package? 

It's currently copyrighted to LangChain (which I don't think is your intention): https://github.com/andrestorres123/breeze-agent/tree/main?tab=MIT-1-ov-file

Author: https://github.com/andrestorres123/breeze-agent/blob/main/pyproject.toml#L6

body:
> The documentation is actually correct -- please use the latest version of `pymongo`

@vbarda 

https://pypi.org/project/langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb/#history

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da8c3bb1-d8f1-450b-83c4-090456bf505b)

cannot  
```
use the latest version of `pymongo`
```

as picture 1 shows, pip's latest version of langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb is 0.1.0

which depends on `pymongo<4.10.0,>=4.9.0

latest version of `pymongo` is 4.11.1

if you try to upgrade pymongo, you would get the error like this:

```
(.venv) E:\workspace\secret>pip install --upgrade pymongo                      
Looking in indexes: (secret)
Requirement already satisfied: pymongo in e:\workspace\secret\.venv\lib\site-packages (4.9.2)
Collecting pymongo
  Using cached http://mirrors.sangfor.org/pypi/packages/pymongo/4.11.1/pymongo-4.11.1-cp311-cp311-win_amd64.whl (831 kB)
Requirement already satisfied: dnspython<3.0.0,>=1.16.0 in e:\workspace\sssssssss\.venv\lib\site-packages (from pymongo) (2.7.0)
Installing collected packages: pymongo
  Attempting uninstall: pymongo
    Found existing installation: pymongo 4.9.2
    Uninstalling pymongo-4.9.2:
      Successfully uninstalled pymongo-4.9.2
ERROR: pip's dependency resolver does not currently take into account all the packages that are installed. This behaviour is the source of the following dependency conflicts.
langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb 0.1.0 requires pymongo<4.10.0,>=4.9.0, but you have pymongo 4.11.1 which is incompatible.
```

just worried, do you guys, happened to forget sync latest codes into pip central? as mongo things seems in another repo...
author: XenoAmess

body:
@vbarda see this. https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-mongodb/commit/1dbfee3354bd39246af35909288b0f9d4d98f2da

sigh.

so before this commit, the real 0.1.0 in central actually can only use pymongo 4.9.x (which is the actual 0.1.0 in your pip central repo.)

I really suggest you use a snapshot version after you release one version & before next release, to make sure which source means which version, but this is python, so as python is just always dirty...sigh

author: benjamincburns

body:
Hi @benjamincburns,

I updated the PR and added the test, but I've run into a problem.
It works ok for `v1` but it fails for `v2`.

It seems that the state that the conditional edge receives is not the full state (but the one in the source node?), so it cannot inject it correctly on the tool.

I don't know if this can be "fixed" somehow.
Any ideas/suggestions??
author: ianchi

body:
Hi @benjamincburns,

I found a "fix" for the v2 problem. Anyhow is more of a hack than a good fix.

Although I couldn't find it clearly in the documentation it seems that currently in Langgraph:
- conditional edges recieve the same state defined in the origin node (either by input, type annotation, or implicit). Type annotation in the conditional function are completely ignored.
- for tools, the type in the `InjectedState` annotation is ignored. The available state is injected as is, with no convertion (as is the case in nodes)

I couldn't find any other more elegant solution, given these conditions.

Hi @xyin-anl! Thanks for contributing! 

I find it really difficult to understand what the library helps to accomplish. In general, we're happy to accept contributions regardless. However, I'd like to understand in more detail in this case b/c the underlying code is doing a bunch of things like ast parsing and evals that do not seem necessary and could introduce security risks.

Could you explain why the code is designed as it it? 

Separately, consider condensing the introduction in the README.md to really the essentials (e.g., 3-5 sentences for the entire overview that explains the core problem). There's a lot of introductory text there, but as a potential user, I still don't know what specific problem the library solves.

Hi @eyurtsev , thanks for reviewing the package and for your thoughtful comments!

Basically, this package provides a simplified syntax/interface for non-professional software developers—like scientists in labs who write code for scientific tasks—to use `langgraph` more easily. It lets them create langgraph workflows using prompt templates or existing functions as nodes, without worrying too much about syntax.

There’s been a growing interest in foundational AI, like LLMs and VLMs, within the scientific community, and many researchers now realize that we need agentic workflows for serious scientific tasks. We’ve found that state machine frameworks like `langgraph` are fantastic for building reliable and robust workflows. Many researchers want to build their own langgraph workflows, but the learning curve is pretty steep for them—so that’s what motivated us to create this framework. Initially, it was just for internal use at Argonne National Lab, but now it’s public!

Regarding your comment on AST parsing and evaluation—yeah, that’s because we’re working on a YAML-based workflow template system, which allows workflows to be represented in YAML. It’s mainly used to load conditions from YAML. I tried to put in enough safeguards by only allowing certain operations, but you’re absolutely right that this could introduce security risks. Hopefully, professional developers can help strengthen this in the future.

As for the README.md, I totally get your point. Right now, it has a lot of introductory content because foundation models, graphs, and state machines are still pretty new concepts for many researchers. The README is kind of serving as a mini-documentation at the moment, but we’re working on building a proper documentation site—once that’s ready, we’ll clean up the README.

For real-world applications, we’ve already published one in [computational imaging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09034), and we’re actively building more workflows internally, with plans to publish more soon. We are also building an [example repository](https://github.com/xyin-anl/nodeology_examples) now to show how to use this package for scientific problems. At the end of the day, this package is built on top of langgraph, so it’s super flexible—just like langgraph itself!

Thanks again for your feedback! Really appreciate it. Let me know if you have any questions.
author: xyin-anl

body: Is there an example that shows off the AST parsing logic?
author: eyurtsev

body:
> Is there an example that shows off the AST parsing logic?

Yes, you can find some example expressions in the [test_workflow.py](https://github.com/xyin-anl/Nodeology/blob/main/tests/test_workflow.py), in functions such as `test_condition_expression_validation` and `test_eval_condition`. For a condition expression in a yaml file, you can check [particle_trajectory_analysis.yaml](https://github.com/xyin-anl/nodeology_examples/blob/main/workflows/particle_trajectory_analysis.yaml) where a simple negation logic is combined with a state value to form a condition expression. Just as you pointed out, for safety concerns only limited types of logics are allowed for now. I have to say the yaml template system hasn't been tested by many users so I hope we will make it better and safer in the future.

body:
@ianchi thanks for adding the test -- I updated it a bit to fix some errors in it.

as you pointed out, pydantic inputs are not supported in `langchain-core` ChatPromptTemplate. we can continue discussion for that in the other PR you created

also, you can simply supply a function as a prompt. would that be sufficient for your use case?

```python
def prompt(state: State):
    return [SystemMessage(content=f"You are an {state.role}.")] + state.messages
```

> injected state in the tool is inconsistent

what do you mean by this? it works as expected for me (when i use prompt function)

as for "forcing to have RemainingStes in the state." - this is actually required for [this part](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/libs/prebuilt/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py#L662) of the code to work, so i think for now we'll keep it as is. note that since these are managed values, they will not show up in the output state
author: vbarda

body:
Hi @vbarda ,

For now I switched back to using TypedDict instead of pydantic in everything langchain/langgraph related, and keep pydantic for all the rest of the application. 

It would be really nice to have better support for it, not only in the react agent, but in general.
But I understand from the comments in the PRs, that it is simply not the native way.

Thanks for all the great work!
author: ianchi

body:
> Hi @vbarda ,
> 
> For now I switched back to using TypedDict instead of pydantic in everything langchain/langgraph related, and keep pydantic for all the rest of the application.
> 
> It would be really nice to have better support for it, not only in the react agent, but in general. But I understand from the comments in the PRs, that it is simply not the native way.
> 
> Thanks for all the great work!

That works too! I would say that LangGraph (the framework) has full support for both Pydantic and TypedDict state schemas. But I agree that it's suboptimal that `ChatPromptTemplate` doesn't handle Pydantic models out of box (which is not an issue with LangGraph, but still annoying -- will look into how to support this properly)

body:
@vbarda is this meant to be a general recommendation? i notice some other places in the documentation where `BaseMessage` is used where perhaps `AnyMessage` is preferred(?) - example: [Tutorial - Agentic RAG](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/tutorials/rag/langgraph_agentic_rag/#agent-state)

Is this too trivial of a distinction to merit a fix? I'm happy to submit a fix for the dozen or so docs (quick estimate from glance with VS-Code find-all) that break this convention.
author: hesreallyhim

body:
Hi @vbarda, @hesreallyhim 
I found this PR and I think there is general problem with having both BaseMessage and AnyMessage.
For example:
Langchain BaseChatModel is using BaseMessage
https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/core/langchain_core/language_models/chat_models.py#L165

Langgraph MessagesState is using AnyMessage
https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/libs/langgraph/langgraph/graph/message.py#L274

The problem is that those definitions are not compatible with each other which results in multiple Mypy errors :(

TL;DR; what are the pros of using AnyMessage here ?
author: maver1ck

body: @maver1ck can you give an example (like a LOC that shows a MyPy error)? I'm still trying to grok the distinction, I know BaseMessage is an ABC, and AnyMessage is a union of subclasses (AIMessage, HumanMessage, etc.), so it has something to do with ABC's not being serializable, and maybe whether there are any methods that are defined in the BaseMessage but not declared in the AnyMessage(?) but yeah would love to know more.
author: hesreallyhim

body: It looks like the AnyMessage union types basically inherit from "BaseMessage" and then define their own `type`. Like `BaseMessage` has a `type` field definition but it's abstract and then `HumanMessage(BaseMessage)` has `type: Literal["human"] = "human"`
author: hesreallyhim

body:
@hesreallyhim 
Yes.
This is original code (not mine but I'm trying to use this template in my project)
https://github.com/JoshuaC215/agent-service-toolkit/blob/main/src/agents/bg_task_agent/bg_task_agent.py

Original code is giving following mypy error:
```
src/agents/bg_task_agent/bg_task_agent.py:26: error: Incompatible return value type (got "RunnableSerializable[AgentState, BaseMessage]", expected "RunnableSerializable[AgentState, AIMessage]")  [return-value]
```
So naturally I'd like to change line 21 to:
```
def wrap_model(model: BaseChatModel) -> RunnableSerializable[AgentState, BaseMessage]:
```

Then I'm getting this which is impossible to fix when using Langchain / Langgraph built-in mechanisms. 
```
src/agents/bg_task_agent/bg_task_agent.py:35: error: List item 0 has incompatible type "BaseMessage"; expected "AIMessage | HumanMessage | ChatMessage | SystemMessage | FunctionMessage | ToolMessage"  [list-item]
```
author: maver1ck

body: @maver1ck sorry I've only skimmed the code so far, and I'd still love someone with deeper context to chime in, but have you tried using `AnyMessage` at the end of 21 instead of `BaseMessage`? I'm not sure why the types are "incompatible" but `AnyMessage` I think is literally an alias for `"AIMessage | HumanMessage | ChatMessage | SystemMessage | FunctionMessage | ToolMessage"`
author: hesreallyhim

body:
@hesreallyhim 
Not working
```
src/agents/bg_task_agent/bg_task_agent.py:27: error: Incompatible return value type (got "RunnableSerializable[AgentState, BaseMessage]", expected "RunnableSerializable[AgentState, AIMessage | HumanMessage | ChatMessage | SystemMessage | FunctionMessage | <7 more items>]")  [return-value]
```

Probably because we're using BaseChatModel from Langchain which is defined using BaseMessage
```
class BaseChatModel(BaseLanguageModel[BaseMessage], ABC):
```

body:
Hey @eyurtsev ,

I've found configuration in the `mkdocs.yml` that allows us to automatically prepend "Added in version" to the version admonitions. Specifically, we've set up the `markdown_version_annotations` plugin with this configuration:

```yaml
- markdown_version_annotations:
    version_added_title: "Added in version \\1"
```

This means when we use `+++ 0.2.24` or `!!! version-added "0.2.24"`, it will automatically generate an admonition that says "Added in version 0.2.24".

Let me know what you think!

body:
@eyurtsev   I checked the history of types.py, and it looks like at some point, the entire file was either moved or significantly changed—including PregelTask, which you mentioned.

I followed your suggested steps and created a release based on that version, but let me know if I misunderstood anything or if there’s a better way to approach it. I just want to make sure the GitHub diff actions correctly reflect when PregelTask was added to the class.

Here are the relevant links for reference:
[GitHub Link 1](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/d9854b36ebb6690a5106ad73a3099ef3ee386259/libs/langgraph/langgraph/types.py)
[GitHub Link 2](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/d9854b36ebb6690a5106ad73a3099ef3ee386259/libs/langgraph/langgraph/types.py)

Let me know what you think!
author: YassinNouh21

body:
Use version-added for when the object / type was introduced into langgraph.

version-modified can be used to capture modifications (e.g., changing namespaces for the type etc.)

body:
Hello! Thanks for your contribution :)

> What is being done in postgres' "migrations"?

These are run when you call `setup()` to create the tables & indices expected by the store. The migrations contain the actual SQL migration code.

> Is there a particular behaviour done on concurrent writes?
> I am getting a DuplicateKeyError in the test in test_pregel.test_store_injected
[test_async_store::test_large_batches](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/libs/checkpoint-postgres/tests/test_async_store.py#L128-L174) highlights the situation.

For concurrent writes, we assume the "last write wins", so if you have a batch containing put ops to create, update , then delete an item, the query would end with the item being deleted. In postgres (and the batch api), we currently deduplicate in python before even creating the query

author: crenus

body:
> Does 3.27 work? with that I no longer get errors whe nI start from langgraph studio, but when it gets to a subgraph expecting AnyMEssage, that still doesnt work. Previously worked on 0.3.24 for me



In version 0.3.27, polymorphic types are stored as raw dictionaries. Therefore, it’s necessary to manually deserialize them into the correct types using BaseModel.model_validate() when handling state objects.

like:
```python
def node(state):
      state.polymorphic = polymorphic_type.model_validate(state.polymorphic)
```

@sydney-runkle  Could you give an example for the RunsClient. stream()
```
    @overload
    def stream(
        self,
        thread_id: str,
        assistant_id: str,
        *,
        input: Optional[dict] = None,
        command: Optional[Command] = None,
        stream_mode: Union[StreamMode, Sequence[StreamMode]] = "values",
        stream_subgraphs: bool = False,
        stream_resumable: bool = False,
        metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
        config: Optional[Config] = None,
        checkpoint: Optional[Checkpoint] = None,
        checkpoint_id: Optional[str] = None,
        checkpoint_during: Optional[bool] = None,
        interrupt_before: Optional[Union[All, Sequence[str]]] = None,
        interrupt_after: Optional[Union[All, Sequence[str]]] = None,
        feedback_keys: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        on_disconnect: Optional[DisconnectMode] = None,
        webhook: Optional[str] = None,
        multitask_strategy: Optional[MultitaskStrategy] = None,
        if_not_exists: Optional[IfNotExists] = None,
        after_seconds: Optional[int] = None,
        headers: Optional[dict[str, str]] = None,
        on_run_created: Optional[Callable[[RunCreateMetadata], None]] = None,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[StreamPart]: ...

    @overload
    def stream(
        self,
        thread_id: None,
        assistant_id: str,
        *,
        input: Optional[dict] = None,
        command: Optional[Command] = None,
        stream_mode: Union[StreamMode, Sequence[StreamMode]] = "values",
        stream_subgraphs: bool = False,
        stream_resumable: bool = False,
        metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
        config: Optional[Config] = None,
        checkpoint_during: Optional[bool] = None,
        interrupt_before: Optional[Union[All, Sequence[str]]] = None,
        interrupt_after: Optional[Union[All, Sequence[str]]] = None,
        feedback_keys: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        on_disconnect: Optional[DisconnectMode] = None,
        on_completion: Optional[OnCompletionBehavior] = None,
        if_not_exists: Optional[IfNotExists] = None,
        webhook: Optional[str] = None,
        after_seconds: Optional[int] = None,
        headers: Optional[dict[str, str]] = None,
        on_run_created: Optional[Callable[[RunCreateMetadata], None]] = None,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[StreamPart]: ...

    def stream(
        self,
        thread_id: Optional[str],
        assistant_id: str,
        *,
        input: Optional[dict] = None,
        command: Optional[Command] = None,
        stream_mode: Union[StreamMode, Sequence[StreamMode]] = "values",
        stream_subgraphs: bool = False,
        stream_resumable: bool = False,
        metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
        config: Optional[Config] = None,
        checkpoint: Optional[Checkpoint] = None,
        checkpoint_id: Optional[str] = None,
        checkpoint_during: Optional[bool] = None,
        interrupt_before: Optional[Union[All, Sequence[str]]] = None,
        interrupt_after: Optional[Union[All, Sequence[str]]] = None,
        feedback_keys: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        on_disconnect: Optional[DisconnectMode] = None,
        on_completion: Optional[OnCompletionBehavior] = None,
        webhook: Optional[str] = None,
        multitask_strategy: Optional[MultitaskStrategy] = None,
        if_not_exists: Optional[IfNotExists] = None,
        after_seconds: Optional[int] = None,
        headers: Optional[dict[str, str]] = None,
        on_run_created: Optional[Callable[[RunCreateMetadata], None]] = None,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[StreamPart]:
        """Create a run and stream the results.

        Args:
            thread_id: the thread ID to assign to the thread.
                If None will create a stateless run.
            assistant_id: The assistant ID or graph name to stream from.
                If using graph name, will default to first assistant created from that graph.
            input: The input to the graph.
            command: A command to execute. Cannot be combined with input.
            stream_mode: The stream mode(s) to use.
            stream_subgraphs: Whether to stream output from subgraphs.
            stream_resumable: Whether the stream is considered resumable.
                If true, the stream can be resumed and replayed in its entirety even after disconnection.
            metadata: Metadata to assign to the run.
            config: The configuration for the assistant.
            checkpoint: The checkpoint to resume from.
            checkpoint_during: Whether to checkpoint during the run (or only at the end/interruption).
            interrupt_before: Nodes to interrupt immediately before they get executed.
            interrupt_after: Nodes to Nodes to interrupt immediately after they get executed.
            feedback_keys: Feedback keys to assign to run.
            on_disconnect: The disconnect mode to use.
                Must be one of 'cancel' or 'continue'.
            on_completion: Whether to delete or keep the thread created for a stateless run.
                Must be one of 'delete' or 'keep'.
            webhook: Webhook to call after LangGraph API call is done.
            multitask_strategy: Multitask strategy to use.
                Must be one of 'reject', 'interrupt', 'rollback', or 'enqueue'.
            if_not_exists: How to handle missing thread. Defaults to 'reject'.
                Must be either 'reject' (raise error if missing), or 'create' (create new thread).
            after_seconds: The number of seconds to wait before starting the run.
                Use to schedule future runs.
            on_run_created: Callback when a run is created.

        Returns:
            AsyncIterator[StreamPart]: Asynchronous iterator of stream results.

        ???+ example "Example Usage"

            ```python
            client = get_client(url="http://localhost:2024)
            async for chunk in client.runs.stream(
                thread_id=None,
                assistant_id="agent",
                input={"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "how are you?"}]},
                stream_mode=["values","debug"],
                metadata={"name":"my_run"},
                config={"configurable": {"model_name": "anthropic"}},
                interrupt_before=["node_to_stop_before_1","node_to_stop_before_2"],
                interrupt_after=["node_to_stop_after_1","node_to_stop_after_2"],
                feedback_keys=["my_feedback_key_1","my_feedback_key_2"],
                webhook="https://my.fake.webhook.com",
                multitask_strategy="interrupt"
            ):
                print(chunk)
            ```

            ```shell

            ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

            StreamPart(event='metadata', data={'run_id': '1ef4a9b8-d7da-679a-a45a-872054341df2'})
            StreamPart(event='values', data={'messages': [{'content': 'how are you?', 'additional_kwargs': {}, 'response_metadata': {}, 'type': 'human', 'name': None, 'id': 'fe0a5778-cfe9-42ee-b807-0adaa1873c10', 'example': False}]})
            StreamPart(event='values', data={'messages': [{'content': 'how are you?', 'additional_kwargs': {}, 'response_metadata': {}, 'type': 'human', 'name': None, 'id': 'fe0a5778-cfe9-42ee-b807-0adaa1873c10', 'example': False}, {'content': "I'm doing well, thanks for asking! I'm an AI assistant created by Anthropic to be helpful, honest, and harmless.", 'additional_kwargs': {}, 'response_metadata': {}, 'type': 'ai', 'name': None, 'id': 'run-159b782c-b679-4830-83c6-cef87798fe8b', 'example': False, 'tool_calls': [], 'invalid_tool_calls': [], 'usage_metadata': None}]})
            StreamPart(event='end', data=None)
            ```

        """  # noqa: E501
        payload = {
            "input": input,
            "command": (
                {k: v for k, v in command.items() if v is not None} if command else None
            ),
            "config": config,
            "metadata": metadata,
            "stream_mode": stream_mode,
            "stream_subgraphs": stream_subgraphs,
            "stream_resumable": stream_resumable,
            "assistant_id": assistant_id,
            "interrupt_before": interrupt_before,
            "interrupt_after": interrupt_after,
            "feedback_keys": feedback_keys,
            "webhook": webhook,
            "checkpoint": checkpoint,
            "checkpoint_id": checkpoint_id,
            "checkpoint_during": checkpoint_during,
            "multitask_strategy": multitask_strategy,
            "if_not_exists": if_not_exists,
            "on_disconnect": on_disconnect,
            "on_completion": on_completion,
            "after_seconds": after_seconds,
        }
        endpoint = (
            f"/threads/{thread_id}/runs/stream"
            if thread_id is not None
            else "/runs/stream"
        )

        def on_response(res: httpx.Response):
            """Callback function to handle the response."""
            if on_run_created and (metadata := _get_run_metadata_from_response(res)):
                on_run_created(metadata)

        return self.http.stream(
            endpoint,
            "POST",
            json={k: v for k, v in payload.items() if v is not None},
            headers=headers,
            on_response=on_response if on_run_created else None,
        )
```

> * This was deprecated, and superseded by checkpoint_during=False, which is available for all checkpointers

I've a question regarding this - what we're noticing with checkpointer is our storage is growing steadily (pace is increasing infact). Thanks in advance!

body:
Please ignore my previous test comment. I think I've found a proper fix.

I was also confused by this, as I was looking at how `astream_events` is implemented in langchain-core. It turns out that for `AzureChatOpenAI`(or your AI client), you can pass `stream_usage=True` as an argument. This correctly populates the usage_metadata in the final `on_chat_model_end` event stream. 

It seems to me that in your case, what happened was that you've added 'messages' stream mode and that causes this issue.

This official documentation confirms it: 
https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/chat_token_usage_tracking/#streaming

https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/openai/chat_models/langchain_openai.chat_models.base.BaseChatOpenAI.html#langchain_openai.chat_models.base.BaseChatOpenAI.stream_usage
author: pedro-inf-custodio

body: Hi @ItsRoy69, closing because this is misguided - OpenAI’s Chat Completions API does not stream token usage statistics by default. As @pedro-inf-custodio mentioned, to recover token counts when streaming with ChatOpenAI or AzureChatOpenAI, set `stream_usage=True` as an initialization parameter or on invocation. [This is documented](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/chat/openai#streaming-usage-metadata).

body:
Hi @leo-gan thanks for the contribution.

The content needs more work before we it can be featured as a tutorial. 

Here's a good reference on how to write tutorials: https://diataxis.fr/tutorials/

Before writing a tutorial, let's establish the learning objective -- i..e, what do we hope a user reading this tutorial to get out of it? (For example, is the goal to show a user how to use the prebuilt agent with tools?)

Then we can evaluate whether the tutorial achieves the stated goal efficiently; i.e., the tutorial is quick to go through while achieving the stated goal.

body:
> I haven't seen evidence that the implementation is correct or producing useful results and have not heard back from @idosal on this PR: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/4502
> 
> The information shown that shows the trace of the agent suggests that the implementation is not correct.

Hey, I'm really sorry, I didn't see the followup.
The MCP server works as expected and provides useful answers in Claude, Cursor, VSCode, etc., where the vast majority of Langgraph questions come from. There have been over 2K users since the badge was added, which demonstrates usefulness.
After examination, the online chat app itself has a bug that prevents it from using the fetch URL tool, which makes it less useful on questions that require pulling extra docs. We're working on upgrading the chat app and will push it within the next few days. Thanks for your patience!

author: sydney-runkle

body:
I've updated all the `uv.lock` files across the monorepo to properly reflect the new dynamic versioning system. Here's what was done:

1. **Ran `uv lock -P <package-name>` for each package** to refresh the lockfiles with dynamic versioning:
   - `langgraph-core` (libs/langgraph)
   - `langgraph-checkpoint` (libs/checkpoint)  
   - `langgraph-prebuilt` (libs/prebuilt)
   - `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres` (libs/checkpoint-postgres)
   - `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` (libs/checkpoint-sqlite)
   - `langgraph-sdk` (libs/sdk-py)
   - `langgraph-cli` (libs/cli)

2. now use `(dynamic)` versioning** in their lockfiles instead of hardcoded version numbers, which means they'll properly use the git-based dynamic versioning at build time.

3. Verified `uv build` works locally - all packages build successfully with the new dynamic versioning system.

@sydney-runkle
author: YassinNouh21

body:
these are the sequence of the commands I used 
```

# Update lockfiles for each package using uv lock -P <package-name>
cd libs/langgraph && uv lock -P langgraph-core
cd ../checkpoint && uv lock -P langgraph-checkpoint  
cd ../prebuilt && uv lock -P langgraph-prebuilt
cd ../checkpoint-postgres && uv lock -P langgraph-checkpoint-postgres
cd ../checkpoint-sqlite && uv lock -P langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite
cd ../sdk-py && uv lock -P langgraph-sdk
cd ../cli && uv lock -P langgraph-cli

# Navigate back to project root
cd ../../

# Check what files were modified
git status

# Add and commit all updated lockfiles
git add libs/*/uv.lock
git commit -m "chore: update lockfiles for dynamic versioning"
```

body:
Thanks for the reply!

I just wanted to clarify the motivation for this PR:

Currently, web_search is triggered even if some documents are relevant — as long as any one document is not. This leads to unnecessary query regeneration and web searches, while potentially overlooking already useful documents.

The updated logic ensures that we only fall back to web search when none of the documents are relevant, which seems like a more precise behavior and avoids redundant operations.

Let me know if you see a different intent behind the original logic — happy to discuss further or adjust the fix.

body: Hey @yoadsn, thank you for your contribution. We'll soon be releasing our new prebuilt agent [`create_agent()`](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/agents) with the upcoming v1.0 LangChain, which will depricate `create_react_agen()t`. Pre-/post-model hooks will be replaced by our new [middleware abstractions](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware), so we aren’t taking new features on that surface. I'm sorry we didn't get to you earlier!

Closing this in favour of #5240

body:
cc @zanieb, if I only want to test against minimum versions of direct dependencies, is there currently a way to do that with `--resolution`?

seems like the whole suite of deps is being re-synced with that flag and things like `--no-dev` are ignored...
author: sydney-runkle

body: Can you point me to the failure? We won't sync groups with `--no-default-groups`, but we will perform a resolution for the whole project still.
author: zanieb

body:
@zanieb, sure thing! thank you for your help!!!

https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/actions/runs/16032573491/job/45236555454

An example - `numpy` is a testing dep here, but just hoping to install min required deps using
```
uv sync --no-default-groups --resolution lowest-direct --no-sources
```
author: sydney-runkle

body:
Yeah so that's a failure during resolve, not install. The lockfile always reflects a solve for the entire project, there's no way to subset it. I think we'd need to introduce a new option to scope resolution modes to different subsets of the graph. It's probably plausible, but I'm not sure how hard it would be to implement.

You can provide static metadata for the problematic version of numpy and we should skip the build: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/resolution/#dependency-metadata
author: zanieb

body:
Thanks for the pointers! Makes sense.

Would love to see such a feature but understand it's pretty niche.
author: sydney-runkle

body: You could also just `uv pip install` for the test, which _won't_ solve for those dependency groups at all.

body:
Hi @nfcampos, sorry to revive this old refactoring, but I'm under the impression this is related to the issue I'm [experiencing](https://forum.langchain.com/t/persisting-hitl-payloads/2950/4). The gist of the issue is that:
- "async" and "sync" saves the state when the next node starts (or after) so it won't persist changes on interrupt graph exit
- "exit" saves the state on interrupt graph exit but won't persist if it doesn't interrupt

Would you know if there's a way to combine "async" _and_ "exit"?

Prepare_tools looks like a good solution as well and could be used to get list of tools not only from config but from state as well for dynamic tools. Let me know if you need help with this refactoring.
author: AydarDD

body:
@AydarAkhmetzyanov I have a PR that implements full dynamic tool selection support for ToolNodes (based on also state, context), but after thinking about it some more I am not sure that any changes should be added to ToolNode b/c they cannot be used without corresponding changes in the chat model!

Could you help me understand a bit more about your use case?

* Are you making a change both in the LLM and in the ToolNode?
* Why is the change in the LLM not sufficient? Are you worried that the LLM provider will output tools that are not in the list of allowed tools? Are you using a custom LLM to call tools?
* Is your architecture completely custom or is it similar to a looping agent? (i.e., would create_react_agent) accommodate your use case?
author: eyurtsev

body:
@eyurtsev
1. LLM with tools can be provided as part of the configuration to graph, the goal of this PR is to enable Tool selection at pre-compilation time so that we can reuse compiled graph with different tools.
2. Because we want to reuse compiled graph for different agents/use cases with agent-specific tools, prompts, llms etc. Esentially, its agentic platform use case. Currently, we have to recompile graph on each LLM call or support a custom ToolNode implementation. Answering to your questions, yes list of tools and llm with tools is execution/call-specific.
3. Yes, we have a custom graph architecture.

Let me provide code sample from our agentic platform, we have to compile the graph at for each run like that:
```
def build_compiled_graph(tools: list):
    graph_builder = StateGraph(State)

    # Add nodes
    ...
    graph_builder.add_node("request_labeling", request_labeling_node)
    graph_builder.add_node("tool_calling_agent", tool_calling_agent_node)
    graph_builder.add_node("tools", ToolNode(
        tools=tools))  # ToolNode doesn't support Configurable unfortunatelly, so we have to build graph each time in runtime
    ...
    
    # Add edges
    ...

    return graph_builder.compile()

def stream_graph(
        ...
) -> Iterator[Union[AIResponse, IntermediateStep]]:
    config = {
        "configurable": {
            "llm": llm,
            "llm_with_tools": llm.bind_tools(tools),
            "system_message": system_message,
            ....
        }}

    graph = build_compiled_graph(tools)
```


If tools can be loaded from `configurable`, the same graph can be reused for different agents and agent runs.

Our code with ToolNode version from this PR:
```
def build_compiled_graph():
    graph_builder = StateGraph(State)

    # Add nodes
    ...
    graph_builder.add_node("request_labeling", request_labeling_node)
    graph_builder.add_node("tool_calling_agent", tool_calling_agent_node)
    graph_builder.add_node("tools", ToolNode(config_tools_key="tools"))
    ...

    # Add edges
    ...

    return graph_builder.compile()

precompiled_graph = build_compiled_graph()

def stream_graph(
        ...
) -> Iterator[Union[AIResponse, IntermediateStep]]:
    config = {
        "configurable": {
            "llm": llm,
            "llm_with_tools": llm.bind_tools(tools),
            "system_message": system_message,
            "tools": tools
            ....
        }}

    graph = precompiled_graph
```
author: AydarDD

We now support runtime configurable tools via the [middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware#modify-model-request) API - currently in alpha.

Going to close this as not planned, as we migrate our agent abstractions to langchain.

Hi @adhishthite, thank you for your contribution.

We currently maintain a handful of official checkpointers with our partners and don't plan to extend this selection at the moment.

If you want to share your implementation in an unofficial capacity, please start a new discussion for that. Either way, we suggest that if an Elasticsearch checkpointer is something you need in your software, you create and maintain your own library. You can migrate over our existing tests, e.g. checkpoint-postgres/tests, to make things easier.

I'm going to close this PR.

body:
> Hi @jitokim,
> 
> Take a look at the type signature of ToolCall. args are required and can be an empty dict to support a parameterless function.
> 
> We cannot/should not update the code here to support missing args given that it's not consistent w/ the tool call type.

Hi @eyurtsev  , Thanks for the clarification.

You're absolutely right that the ToolCall type requires args, and that a missing field is technically invalid.
Since LangGraph (e.g., in [#5722](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/issues/5722)) may emit tool calls without args when a tool has no parameters, this results in unintended validation errors.

To align with the ToolCall spec and avoid relaxing LangGraph's schema, I’ve opened a PR in LangChain to patch this at the source by defaulting args to {} if missing:

https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/32408

Given that, I think it's best to close this PR on the LangGraph side. Thanks again!
author: jitokim

body:
> Since LangGraph (e.g., in https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/issues/5722) may emit tool calls without args when a tool has no parameters, this results in unintended validation errors.

We need to fix the root cause instead of adjusting the schema in langchain. The langchain schema is correct.

Could we determine whether the issue is in LangGraph or ChatOpenAI?

Based on the issue that you've referenced, it appears that the issue is actually that someone is using a NON open ai model via the ChatOpenAI interface and that model API is actually complying with the openai completions API.

If so, we'll need to make the adjustment for this in ChatOpenAI for the logic that generates the AIMessage that has tool calls
author: eyurtsev
